answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation includes MACl at 0.3 mg/mL in the perovskite precursor solution (Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉I₂.₉Br₀.₁, 1.73 mol/L) alongside MeO-4PADBC (0.33 mg/mL) as a SAM. While MACl aids crystallization by modulating intermediate phases during film formation, its small ionic radius limits deep defect passivation at grain boundaries and interfaces. This results in significant non-radiative recombination, evidenced by the modest VOC of 1.0105 V and FF of 71.315%, as undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions and halide vacancies persist. Additionally, MACl’s volatility contributes to pinhole formation during annealing, increasing shunt paths that suppress FF and JSC (20.561 mA/cm²). The SAM partially mitigates interfacial energy mismatches but cannot compensate for bulk and grain boundary defects originating from inadequate passivation.

Replacing MACl with PMACl at an identical concentration (0.3 mg/mL) addresses these limitations through steric and electronic effects. PMACl’s phenylmethylammonium cation, with its bulky aromatic group, preferentially segregates at perovskite grain boundaries and surfaces rather than incorporating into the lattice. This passivates deep-level traps by bonding with undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions via its amine group while suppressing halide migration through hydrophobic phenyl barriers. The reduced trap density diminishes Shockley-Read-Hall recombination, directly elevating VOC. Concurrently, PMACl enhances crystallization kinetics, yielding larger grains with fewer pinholes, which lowers series resistance and improves charge extraction—boosting FF and JSC. Although the insulating phenyl groups slightly impede inter-grain transport, the net reduction in recombination losses outweighs this trade-off, as confirmed by performance gains. The SAM concentration remains unchanged, as its role in energy-level alignment is already optimized and independent of bulk passivation.

The optimized formulation achieves a VOC between 1.044 V and 1.084 V, a JSC between 22.77 mA/cm² and 23.17 mA/cm², an FF between 73.32% and 75.32%, and a PCE between 17.4% and 18.9%. These improvements stem directly from suppressed recombination and enhanced film homogeneity. For implementation: replace MACl with PMACl at 0.3 mg/mL in the perovskite precursor solution while retaining all other components and concentrations unchanged.
control_device_fabrication: The PCE for the device reached 14.817%, with a JSC of 20.561 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.0105 V and a FF of 71.315%. 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solutions were prepared with the chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1. Incorporating MeO-4PADBC (0.33 mg/mL) as a SAM was critical to adjust interfacial energy levels and refine the perovskite interface. 0.3 mg/mL MACl was added to the perovskite precursor solution and stirred for 2 h. The perovskite precursor solution was deposited on the substrate via a two-step spin coating process; first, the solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. After 6 s into the second stage, 160 µL CB antisolvent was dropped on top of the spinning substrates. The films were then annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
